content.title: About
content.content: Puerto Rican style meatballs are small balls made from ground meat (usually beef or pork) seasoned with classic island spices: adobo, cumin, oregano, garlic and fresh cilantro. They are pan‑fried until golden and commonly served with rice, beans and fried plantains.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The recipe dates back to the early 20th century, when Spanish colonists adapted their meatball dishes to local ingredients.
Puerto Rican cuisine often uses adobo sauce, giving the meatballs a characteristic reddish hue and a subtle smoky flavor.
Traditional preparation may involve cooking the meatballs in earthenware pots, which retain moisture and aroma.
The dish is popular both at home and in street stalls, where it is served as “pinchos” – bite‑size portions on skewers.
Puerto Rican meatballs are frequently accompanied by “mojo” sauce, a blend of tomatoes, cream and hot pepper.

items.title: High in protein
items.content: Ground beef or pork provides high‑quality protein essential for muscle growth and repair.

items.title: Contains iron
items.content: Red meat is a good source of heme iron, which is readily absorbed by the body.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: The meat and spices supply B12, niacin and riboflavin, supporting energy metabolism.

items.title: Antioxidants from spices
items.content: Cumin, oregano and garlic contain antioxidant compounds that help protect cells.

items.title: Digestive support
items.content: Cilantro and garlic stimulate bile production, aiding digestion.

items.title: High fat content
items.content: Using fatty cuts can make the dish calorie‑dense; leaner meat is recommended for a lighter version.

items.title: Sodium level
items.content: Salt in the spice mix and sauces can increase sodium intake, which may be a concern for hypertension.

items.title: Spice allergy
items.content: Some individuals may be allergic to cumin, oregano or garlic.

items.title: Food‑borne illness risk
items.content: Undercooked meatballs may harbor pathogens; cook to an internal temperature of 71 °C (160 °F).

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the meatballs hot, often alongside rice, black beans, fried plantains, or as a filling for tacos. They also work well in soups, salads or sandwiches.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep cooked meatballs in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3‑4 days. For longer storage, freeze in portioned bags for up to 2 months. Reheat thoroughly before serving.
